spec.title: Ecommerce – RED
spec.description: Service RED, control-plane and pod health, ingress, capacity, and the logs and traces behind them. Generated by build_ecommerce_red.py.

spec.name: namespace
spec.label: Namespace
spec.description: Filters the pod-health and pod-resources rows.

spec.name: pod
spec.label: Pod (logs)
spec.description: Filters the logs row (ecommerce-dev and monitoring pods).

spec.name: search
spec.label: Log search (regex)
spec.description: Case-insensitive regex applied to the log panels. Empty = everything.

spec.expr:
100 *
sum by (service) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{namespace="ecommerce-dev", service=~"$service", route!~"/health|/metrics", status_code=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval]))
/
sum by (service) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{namespace="ecommerce-dev", service=~"$service", route!~"/health|/metrics"}[$__rate_interval]))

100 *
sum by (service) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{namespace="ecommerce-dev", service=~"$service", route!~"/health|/metrics", status_code=~"4.."}[$__rate_interval]))
/
sum by (service) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count{namespace="ecommerce-dev", service=~"$service", route!~"/health|/metrics"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.title: Event-loop lag p99 by service
spec.description: Time a callback waited for the single Node.js thread. Every request on that pod pays it. Sustained > 100ms means the process is CPU-starved or blocked. Alert: > 200ms for 5m.

spec.title: Control plane components
spec.description: UP/DOWN per control-plane component. API server, CoreDNS and kubelets: can Prometheus scrape them (`up`). etcd, scheduler, controller-manager, kube-proxy, kindnet, metrics-server: is their pod Ready (kube-state-metrics) -- kind binds their metrics to localhost, so they are not scraped. Multi-instance components show DOWN if ANY instance is down. Alert: any tile == 0 for 2m.

spec.title: Nodes
spec.description: Node readiness and kubelet-reported pressure. Alert: Not ready > 0 or Under pressure > 0 for 5m.

spec.title: Pods ($namespace)
spec.description: Pod counts by state for the selected namespaces. Every tile except Running should be 0. Alerts: CrashLoopBackOff > 0 for 5m; Not ready > 0 for 10m; Restarts (1h) > 3 per pod.

spec.expr:
count(
  (kube_pod_status_ready{namespace=~"$namespace",condition="true"} == 0)
  unless on (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase="Succeeded"} == 1)
) or vector(0)

spec.title: Pod health — all pods in $namespace
spec.description: Every pod with its node, phase, readiness and restarts. Built from four kube-state-metrics queries merged on (namespace, pod). Sorted with not-ready pods first. Restarts (1h) is the column to alert on; the lifetime total only tells you a pod has a history.

spec.title: Unhealthy pods right now
spec.description: Only pods with a problem: a waiting reason (CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, CreateContainerConfigError...), not Ready, or a container that RESTARTED IN THE LAST HOUR after exiting OOMKilled/Error. The restart condition matters: last_terminated_reason is kept forever once a container has ever restarted, so without it pods that are healthy today (restarted by a node reboot weeks ago) show up -- six did on this cluster. Empty means healthy. This table is the shape of a good pod alert: the reason label tells the on-call what is broken.

spec.expr:
max by (namespace, pod, reason) (kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{namespace=~"$namespace"} == 1)
or
max by (namespace, pod, reason) (
  label_replace(
    (kube_pod_status_ready{namespace=~"$namespace",condition="true"} == 0)
      unless on (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase="Succeeded"} == 1),
    "reason", "NotReady", "", "")
)
or
max by (namespace, pod, reason) (
  (kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{namespace=~"$namespace",reason=~"OOMKilled|Error"} == 1)
  and on (namespace, pod, container)
  (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[1h]) > 0)
)

spec.title: API server — 5xx error %
spec.description: Share of Kubernetes API requests failing server-side. A sick API server breaks deploys, HPA and every controller at once. Alert: > 1% for 10m.

spec.title: API server — p99 latency (excl. WATCH)
spec.description: p99 per verb. WATCH and CONNECT are long-lived by design and would read as 'slow' forever, so they are excluded. Alert: mutating verbs p99 > 1s for 10m.

spec.title: Ingress controller
spec.description: Controller scraped: Prometheus can reach :10254. Last config reload OK: the most recent nginx.conf reload succeeded -- when it is 0, nginx keeps serving the OLD config, so new Ingress rules silently do nothing. Alert: either == 0 for 5m.

spec.title: Ingress — now
spec.description: Edge view of the whole site: what users experience before any service is involved.

spec.title: Ingress — requests/s by ingress & status class
spec.description: Traffic per Ingress split into 2xx/3xx/4xx/5xx. A rising 4xx band usually means a client or routing problem; 5xx means the backend or nginx itself.

spec.title: Ingress — 5xx error % by ingress
spec.description: Error ratio at the edge. The `or ... * 0` keeps a flat 0 line when there are no 5xx, instead of no line at all. Alert: > 1% for 5m (pair with a minimum request rate so one failed request at 3am does not page).

spec.expr:
100 * (
  sum by (ingress) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{job="ingress-nginx-controller-metrics",status=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval]))
  or sum by (ingress) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{job="ingress-nginx-controller-metrics"}[$__rate_interval])) * 0
) / sum by (ingress) (rate(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{job="ingress-nginx-controller-metrics"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.title: Ingress — latency p95 / p99 by ingress
spec.description: Total time nginx spent on the request, including the upstream. Red line = the 500ms latency threshold used everywhere else on this dashboard.

spec.title: Refused & absorbed — last 15m
spec.description: Edge 429s: ingress-nginx refused a client over 20 rps (burst 100). Per-IP throttles: user-service refused >20 logins/min or >10 registrations/10min from one address. Locked-account attempts: tries against an account locked after 5 wrong passwords. Duplicate checkouts absorbed: retries/double-clicks that would have been second orders before the Idempotency-Key. Alerts: failed logins > 50 in 15m (credential stuffing); locked-account attempts > 20 in 15m; edge 429s sustained 10m.

spec.title: Throttled requests — where they were refused
spec.description: Two layers. The edge refuses floods before any app code runs; user-service refuses credential guessing the edge cannot see (20 rps is plenty for a slow password spray). Edge-only = a noisy client; account_locked = someone targeting accounts.

spec.title: Login outcomes
spec.description: failure rising with success flat = guessing; failure and success both rising = a traffic spike. Upgrades fall to zero as every pre-v2.7 account has logged in once.

spec.title: Checkout idempotency
spec.description: processed = first request for a key; replayed = a retry answered from the stored order; in_progress = a double-click while the first was running; mismatch = a client reusing a key for a different cart (a client bug -- should be 0).

spec.title: Rejected input (400) by route
spec.description: Requests refused by the Zod schemas (or malformed JSON). A sudden rise on one route right after a frontend deploy usually means the client and API disagree on a field.

spec.title: Orders & stock — last 15m
spec.description: Checkouts = orders created (pending_payment). Confirmed = moved to paid. Refused: out of stock = a checkout that would have oversold before v2.8. Reservations expired = stock held for an order that was never confirmed and was returned by the sweeper -- normally 0 until online payment exists. Stock release failures = a cancelled order whose units could NOT be returned (they are missing from the shelf). Alerts: release failures > 0 (page); expired > 0 sustained; out-of-stock rate rising.

spec.title: Stock on hand — units available to reserve
spec.description: Live stock from the shared store. Red at 0 = sold out (checkouts refused); orange under 10 = restock soon. Alert: any product at 0 for 30m.

spec.title: Order status changes
spec.description: Every lifecycle change by target status. pending_payment and paid should track each other closely; a growing gap means confirmations are failing. The k6 run cancels each of its own orders, so cancelled follows paid while it runs.

spec.title: Stock reservations
spec.description: held = stock taken for a new order; committed = sold; released = returned on cancel; expired = returned by the sweeper; out_of_stock = refused.

spec.title: Cluster CPU — usage / requests / limits
spec.description: All as % of allocatable CPU across nodes. REQUESTS is what the scheduler has promised away: near 100% means new pods go Pending even if Usage is low. LIMITS above 100% is overcommit -- fine for CPU (it throttles), so watch Requests. Alert: Requests > 85%.

spec.expr:
100 * sum(kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="cpu"} * on (namespace, pod) group_left() max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase=~"Pending|Running"} == 1))
/ sum(kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="cpu"})

100 * sum(kube_pod_container_resource_limits{resource="cpu"} * on (namespace, pod) group_left() max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase=~"Pending|Running"} == 1))
/ sum(kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="cpu"})

spec.title: Cluster memory — usage / requests / limits
spec.description: All as % of allocatable memory. Usage is working set, the number the kubelet uses for eviction. Memory LIMITS above 100% is dangerous in a way CPU is not: memory cannot be throttled, so overcommitted pods get OOMKilled when they all grow at once. Alerts: Usage > 85%; Limits > 100% as a warning.

spec.expr:
100 * sum(kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="memory"} * on (namespace, pod) group_left() max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase=~"Pending|Running"} == 1))
/ sum(kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="memory"})

100 * sum(kube_pod_container_resource_limits{resource="memory"} * on (namespace, pod) group_left() max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase=~"Pending|Running"} == 1))
/ sum(kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="memory"})

spec.title: Per node — CPU and memory used
spec.description: From node-exporter, so it includes the OS and kubelet, not just pods. One hot node with a cool cluster average is a scheduling/affinity problem, not a capacity one.

defaults.noValue: no pods with this resource set

spec.title: Pods missing requests / limits ($namespace)
spec.description: Pods with no CPU request are invisible to the scheduler's accounting; pods with no memory limit can consume a whole node. They also never appear in the bars above.

spec.expr: count(max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace"}) unless on (namespace, pod) kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="cpu"}) or vector(0)
count(max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_info{namespace=~"$namespace"}) unless on (namespace, pod) kube_pod_container_resource_limits{resource="memory"}) or vector(0)

spec.title: CPU used — % of request
spec.description: Per pod. Consistently < 20% = request too high (wasted reservation). Consistently > 100% = request too low (scheduler is placing it on false information).

spec.expr:
sort_desc(100 *
  sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace=~"$namespace",container!="",image!=""}[$__rate_interval]))
/ sum by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace=~"$namespace",resource="cpu"}))

defaults.noValue: no pods with this resource set

spec.title: CPU used — % of limit
spec.description: Per pod. Near 100% the container is being CPU-throttled: latency rises with no error anywhere. Alert: > 90% for 15m.

spec.expr:
sort_desc(100 *
  sum by (namespace, pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace=~"$namespace",container!="",image!=""}[$__rate_interval]))
/ sum by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace=~"$namespace",resource="cpu"}))

defaults.noValue: no pods with this resource set

spec.title: Memory used — % of request
spec.description: Per pod. Pods above 100% of their memory request are the first evicted when a node runs short.

spec.expr:
sort_desc(100 *
  sum by (namespace, pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace=~"$namespace",container!="",image!=""})
/ sum by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace=~"$namespace",resource="memory"}))

defaults.noValue: no pods with this resource set

spec.title: Memory used — % of limit
spec.description: Per pod. THE OOMKill early-warning: at 100% the kernel kills the container. Alert: > 90% for 10m.

spec.expr:
sort_desc(100 *
  sum by (namespace, pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace=~"$namespace",container!="",image!=""})
/ sum by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace=~"$namespace",resource="memory"}))

defaults.noValue: no pods with this resource set

spec.title: Autoscaling — now ($namespace)
spec.description: At max replicas: the autoscaler has hit its ceiling, so any more load becomes latency. Wants more pods: desired > current -- usually new pods are Pending because the cluster has no room (check Requests on the CPU/memory gauges). Cannot scale: the HPA has no metric to act on (metrics-server down, or a missing resource request) and is frozen. Scale events: many changes in 30m means flapping. Alerts: At max for 15m; Wants more for 10m; Cannot scale for 5m; scale events > 6 in 30m.

spec.expr: count(max by (namespace, horizontalpodautoscaler) (kube_horizontalpodautoscaler_status_current_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"}) >= on (namespace, horizontalpodautoscaler) max by (namespace, horizontalpodautoscaler) (kube_horizontalpodautoscaler_spec_max_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"})) or vector(0)

count(max by (namespace, horizontalpodautoscaler) (kube_horizontalpodautoscaler_status_desired_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"}) > on (namespace, horizontalpodautoscaler) max by (namespace, horizontalpodautoscaler) (kube_horizontalpodautoscaler_status_current_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"})) or vector(0)

spec.title: HPA status — $namespace
spec.description: One row per autoscaler. CPU % and Memory % are the AVERAGE utilisation across the target's pods, as a percentage of their REQUESTS -- which is why an HPA is only as good as the requests it divides by. '% of max' near 100 means no headroom left. Metrics OK = ScalingActive (the HPA can read its metric). At limit = ScalingLimited (desired was clamped to min or max).

spec.expr: 100 * max by (namespace, horizontalpodautoscaler) (kube_horizontalpodautoscaler_status_current_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"}) / on (namespace, horizontalpodautoscaler) max by (namespace, horizontalpodautoscaler) (kube_horizontalpodautoscaler_spec_max_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace"})

spec.title: Replicas over time — current vs desired
spec.description: Solid = running replicas, dashed = what the HPA wants. A dashed line sitting ABOVE its solid line means the HPA asked for pods that did not start (Pending -- no capacity). A sawtooth means flapping: lengthen behavior.scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds.

spec.title: HPA CPU utilisation vs target
spec.description: Average cpu utilisation the HPA sees (% of request); dashed = its target. Above the dashed line the HPA adds pods; well below it, it removes them once the scale-down stabilisation window has passed.

spec.title: HPA memory utilisation vs target
spec.description: Average memory utilisation the HPA sees (% of request); dashed = its target. Above the dashed line the HPA adds pods; well below it, it removes them once the scale-down stabilisation window has passed.

spec.title: Log lines/s by namespace & app
spec.description: Volume, not content. A sudden step usually means a retry loop or a new noisy log statement -- and it is what Loki bills you for.

spec.title: Error-level log lines/s by app
spec.description: Lines whose level is error/err/fatal, in JSON or logfmt. Candidate for a Loki ruler alert: rate > 0.1/s for 10m on any app.

spec.title: Logs — ecommerce-dev
spec.description: Live logs from every pod in ecommerce-dev. Use the Pod and Search variables at the top; Search is a case-insensitive regex.

spec.title: Logs — monitoring
spec.description: Live logs from every pod in monitoring -- Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, Alloy. Look here first when a panel above is empty.

spec.title: Recent traces — ecommerce-dev
spec.description: Click a Trace ID to open the waterfall. This is a 10% sample of healthy traffic plus everything errored or slow.

defaults.noValue: No traces in this time range

spec.title: Error traces — ecommerce-dev
spec.description: Every trace containing a failed span. Complete, not sampled -- the gateway keeps 100% of these.

defaults.noValue: No traces in this time range

spec.title: Slow traces (> 500ms) — ecommerce-dev
spec.description: Every trace over the latency threshold. Complete, not sampled.

defaults.noValue: No traces in this time range

spec.title: Recent traces — monitoring
spec.description: Grafana traces itself into the same pipeline (grafana.ini tracing.opentelemetry in kube-prometheus-stack-values.yaml). A slow dashboard shows here as a slow Grafana trace, with the datasource call that took the time.

defaults.noValue: No traces in this time range
